page: Microsoft Azure M128-64ms is a memory-optimized server instance belonging to the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8280L processor operating at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with 3892.0 GB of system memory, providing 60.81 GB of RAM per core, and includes 4194 GB of local storage. No GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance split between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core CPU performance is weak, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression scoring in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested servers. Conversely, multi-core performance is average, and the server demonstrates strong memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks, reaching 302.69 GB/sec for reads and 155.48 GB/sec for writes. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is also strong, performing in the top 25%.

The qualitative cost profile of the M128-64ms reflects its high resource density, specifically its massive memory-to-vCPU ratio. While single-threaded tasks are inefficient on this hardware, the high memory capacity and strong large-block memory bandwidth make it highly efficient for memory-bound workloads. This server is suited for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise applications with massive memory footprints, and heavy multi-threaded data processing tasks that can leverage the 3892.0 GB RAM array.
